- **Primary engine:** *Owner free cash flow (AOCF) DCF, discounted at cost of equity.* AOCF = operating cash flow − SBC − capex. This is the framework's blessed owner-earnings definition: it starts from filed OCF, subtracts SBC as a real cost (per Section 5 note), and subtracts capex. Because US-GAAP OCF already nets interest paid, AOCF is an equity-side flow — so I discount at **cost of equity** and derive equity value directly (no net-debt subtraction, avoiding double-count).
- **Cross-check engine:** *FCFF at WACC.* FCFF = AOCF + after-tax interest; EV = PV(FCFF) at WACC; equity = EV − net debt ($81M).

Neither is established; the company's own commentary describes organic growth as murky and deal cycles as below normal.

**Execution plan:**

- Set a hard review trigger: any FY2027 guide below ~+8% revenue or an OCF-margin quarter below ~24% is evidence the market's premium multiple is unjustified and the stock is a candidate for exit rather than averaging down.

The market is not wrong that Digi is a better business today than its trailing GAAP earnings suggest — cash conversion and margins have genuinely improved. But at $74.91 the price has already collected that improvement and more. The risk/reward is **unfavorable: roughly 12% downside to fair value on the base case, ~13% downside to the bull case, and ~47% downside to the bear case**, versus ~13% upside only if the bull case fully materializes. Discipline says: **do not buy; hold with caution; buy the gap, not the momentum.**

I use a **10-year explicit-period unlevered DCF on normalized owner free cash flow**, plus a Gordon terminal value. Cash-flow definition:

**FCF = Adj EBITDA − SBC − cash taxes − capex − ΔWC**

I start from **adjusted EBITDA** (the metric management guides and reports, $146.75M FY2026 midpoint) and subtract *only real cash items* (SBC, cash taxes, capex, working-capital change). This deliberately avoids the D&A/capex mismatch that plagues an EBIT-based build for a company whose D&A (~7.9% of revenue, largely acquired-intangible amortization) runs far above capex (~0.7%): the intangibles being amortized were paid for in past acquisitions, so the amortization is not "free" future cash. Modeling from EBITDA + cash deductions keeps the cash-flow base honest and lets me test the D&A treatment separately.
